recipes.name: Tartar Sauce
ingredients_raw: salt and white pepper to taste

steps.text: In a small bowl, mix together mayonnaise, sweet pickle relish, capers, and egg. Season to taste with salt and white pepper. Add a dash of Worcestershire sauce and a dash hot pepper sauce. Stir. Chill.

raw_recipe.headline: Tartar Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This tartar sauce with egg recipe is made with mayonnaise, sweet pickle relish, Worcestershire sauce, capers, and of course, hardboiled eggs.

review.reviewBody: I started to rate this the first time we had it; it was so good. But I wanted to play with it a bit. This is what I found out: 1) I can't improve it. 2) The capers are a nice touch. 3) I've tried it with and without the egg and cannot tell the difference. And since simpler is better in my kitchen, I usually leave it out. 4) I think salmon has an affinity for dill, so I sub dill relish for the sweet relish with salmon. Delicious that way, too. Many thanks, Diane.

I was relieved to find this recipe, after reading all of the others on this recipe site. (I didn't think you could make tartar sauce without capers and hard boiled eggs). This recipe is similar to our family recipe, with only a few easy additions. We use only Helmanns Real Mayonaise, and add the following "spice it up" ingredients: a little creole or dijon mustard and "Old Bay" seasoning. I prefer to rinse the "sweet" flavor from the pickle relish/just run it under faucet in a tea strainer, but be sure to press the water out.

Five stars with caveats - first batch far too sweet & salty:
(1) Sweet relish is *too* sweet; second time I used ground rind (avoids fluid & seeds from the core) from low sodium dill spears. 
(2) Use the lowest sodium good quality mayo you can find. 
*SO* much better than commercial blends! THANKS for sharing !!
Really good recipe. Even better I think with 1 tablespoon of dill weed and 1 teaspoon of lemon zest.

Very good tartar sauce. I left out the egg, and added a couple more dashes of hot sauce. My friends thoroughly enjoyed it. One suggestion: make it the night before. the flavors meld much better than chilling for 30 minutes.

The recipe is good as it is ,but humbly I left out the capers and the Worcestershire sauce , and added normal sugar to increase flavor a dash of dry white wine and a tip spoon of Dijon Mustard, those ingredients are part of my secret recipe that comes from my already dead Grandma , my recipe is almost 130 years old.

I made this with a few substitutes. I don’t usually do this on the first go round on a recipe but I’m not a white pepper fan and I didn’t have any green relish. I substituted black pepper and I minced some homemade bread and butter pickles. Turned out amazing with a walleye fish fry!

This is the tartar sauce I've always wanted to make. The only adjustment I may make in the future is allowing the pickle relish to sit in a strainer to drain off some liquid, or toss a few sweet pickles in the food processor. It was just a tad too thin. Other than that, perfect!

Too much relish. I've always loved sweet relish (even on hot dogs and hamburgers). But I would scale back on the relish in this recipe.

I guess this recipe is for people whom don't really like mayo. I love mayo just by itself if it's a GOOD mayo. I made this tartar sauce with DUKES mayo so maybe that changed the flavor since it doesn't have sugar.

In the past I used to use Best Foods Mayo with just sweet relish, and I really enjoyed that a lot more than this recipe. I really wanted to like this recipe since I LOVE all everything this recipe... heck I even like to eat hard boiled eggs with worcestershire sauce and I love capers with any seafood.... but with this recipe all I taste is relish.
I substituted tangy relish instead of sweet. I will definitely make this again.
Great tartar sauce! I leave out the egg and use some lemon pepper instead of salt & white pepper! Better than anything I have had from a store or restaurant!!!
I’ve made this twice now and this is fabulous!!! I have not made it using an egg. I don’t think I’ll ever buy tartar sauce from the store again! Well worth the effort.
This is the only tarter sausage I make! It is wondweful and I made NO changes. Thank you for this recipe!1

Wow! Wish I had known how easy it is to make tartar sauce. This recipe is awesome. Best I have ever had. I had capers on hand from a previous recipe, so that was easy enough. Never knew capers were used in tartar sauce. I highly recommend this recipe!!
Capers are the key, great flavor. Did not add egg.
Made without the egg & was still delicious. Definitely the recipe I will use from now on.
Followed recipe. Wouldn't change a thing.
Fantastic
I made it . It was easy and very tasty. I added a dash of Franks hot sauce. Please double the recipe because it goes pretty fast.

The only change I made was to double the recipe and I should have tripled it. I will not purchase commercial Tartar sauce again. I can't say enough about this sauce. Someone mentioned chilling it for several hours prior to serving and I agree with that.
